newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Unilever to shed 70 jobs in Netherlands.
newsitem.headline: Unilever to shed 70 jobs in Netherlands.

text.p: Unilever said on Wednesday that the integration of two of its business in The Netherlands would mean the loss of some 70 jobs.
In a brief statement, the group said it planned to fully integrate its Rotterdam-based Van den Bergh unit with its UVG business in Oss in the southern Netherlands by January 1997.
The new entity, Van den Bergh Nederland, will be one of the biggest foods businesses in the Netherlands employing some 2,000 staff at five locations.
Annual sales are slated at around 1.6 billion guilders.
The group will sell margarines, shortenings and frying fats, soups, sauces and dressings, iced tea and speciality meat products.
On Monday Van den Bergh linked its U.S. businesses with those of Thomas J. Lipton, creating a new entity with annual sales of $3 billion.
Unilever said the moves to combine consumer and food service businesses will allow the group to compete more effectively and provide higher value.
